articles.topic: omega-3 aspirin severe gum disease treatment
articles.headline: Omega-3 and Aspirin Match Antibiotics for Gum Disease
articles.body: A year-long study of 109 patients found that combining omega-3 (3g daily) with low-dose aspirin worked nearly as well as antibiotics for treating severe gum disease. About 58% of patients on antibiotics hit the treatment target, compared to 57.7% taking omega-3 and aspirin. Only 23% of the placebo group succeeded. The findings suggest a potential alternative for antibiotic-resistant cases, though more research is needed before replacing standard antibiotics. Researchers emphasize this should always be paired with professional scaling.
articles.takeaway: If you're dealing with severe gum disease, omega-3 and aspirin deserve a conversation with your dentist as a potential complement to standard care.

articles.topic: vitamin D deficiency pain recovery surgery
articles.headline: Low Vitamin D Triples Pain After Surgery. New Study Reveals Why.
articles.body: Women undergoing breast cancer surgery with vitamin D deficiency experienced three times more moderate to severe pain in the first 24 hours after surgery. They also used significantly more opioid painkillers and reported more nausea. Researchers found vitamin D plays a role in how your body senses and manages pain, likely through its anti-inflammatory properties. The findings suggest checking and possibly supplementing vitamin D before major surgery could meaningfully reduce postoperative pain and opioid dependency. This matters for anyone facing planned surgery.
articles.takeaway: Ask your doctor about vitamin D levels before scheduled surgery. It could change your entire recovery experience.

articles.topic: aerobic exercise cardio fitness cognition brain
articles.headline: Your Cardio Fitness Just Became Your Brain's Best Defender
articles.body: New research shows aerobic fitness protects your brain structure and cognitive function as you age. <cite index="57-2,57-3">Exercise increases brain-derived neurotrophic factor, which helps neurons survive and boosts learning and memory. Strong aerobic fitness supports mitochondria, which are key to healthy brain function.</cite> Studies on older adults find that those with higher VO2max (a measure of aerobic capacity) maintain better verbal memory and cognitive sharpness. The connection is clear: the fitness that protects your heart also shields your mind. You don't need extreme training—consistent moderate cardio delivers the brain benefits.
articles.takeaway: Three 30-minute cardio sessions per week isn't just about your heart. It's an investment in your cognition.

articles.topic: ADHD antihypertensive medication heart failure stroke risk
articles.headline: ADHD Patients on Blood Pressure Meds Face Higher Heart Risk
articles.body: <cite index="67-1,67-5">Adults with ADHD had higher adjusted rates of heart failure hospitalization and stroke after antihypertensive medication initiation.</cite> A major Dutch study tracking 706,000 people found those with ADHD starting blood pressure medications had 46% higher heart failure risk and 19% higher stroke risk over time. This isn't about the ADHD meds themselves—it's about how the condition and blood pressure together affect the heart long-term. If you have ADHD and hypertension, this means closer monitoring with your cardiologist matters even more. The good news: awareness lets you take preventive steps earlier.
articles.takeaway: ADHD plus hypertension requires proactive cardiovascular monitoring. Talk to your doctor about your individual risk profile.

workout.title: Dumbbell Press & Bodyweight Push Superset: Compound Density
workout.tip: Rest 60–90 seconds between supersets, not between exercises within a pair. This keeps heart rate elevated for conditioning while allowing local muscle recovery for quality reps on the second movement.
workout.warmup: 3 min: 8 arm circles each way, 6 band pull-aparts (or air resistance rows), 10 cat-cows, 5 inchworms, 5 light dumbbell presses

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bench Press + Push-Up Superset
exercises.reps: 8 DB press / 8 push-ups (incline or knee, as tolerated)
exercises.notes: Complete 8 dumbbell bench presses immediately followed by 8 push-ups with minimal rest. This pairing fatigues the pressing pattern while the second movement reinforces positioning under load. Rest 75 sec before the next superset.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Overhead Press + Incline Push-Up Superset
exercises.notes: Standing DB press into incline push-ups (hands elevated) targets anterior shoulders and upper chest simultaneously. The lighter load of incline push-ups allows fatigue management; pause 1 sec at bottom of each push-up.

workout.cooldown: 4 min: 30 sec shoulder roll and cross-body shoulder stretch, 30 sec pec stretch at doorway each side, 30 sec tricep stretch, 30 sec forward fold with shoulder width legs
workout.description: A superset pairing of dumbbell pressing and push-up variations to build pressing endurance and muscular resilience under moderate volume. Alternating between loaded and bodyweight work allows skill practice while managing fatigue, making it accessible for true beginners establishing movement quality.

meal.title: Italian Whole Grain Polenta Bowl with Poached Eggs & Roasted Tomatoes
meal.description: Creamy, buttery polenta made with whole grain cornmeal provides steady carbohydrate fuel, topped with protein-rich poached eggs and sweet roasted cherry tomatoes for a savory Italian-inspired breakfast. Perfect for endurance athletes who want something filling and digestion-friendly before long training days.
ingredients: salt and black pepper to taste
meal.instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 425°F. Toss cherry tomatoes with olive oil, balsamic vinegar, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 15 minutes until blistered.
2. Meanwhile, bring vegetable broth to a gentle boil in a small pot. Slowly whisk in polenta, stirring constantly to avoid lumps.
3. Reduce heat to low and continue stirring for 15–20 minutes until polenta is creamy and pulls away slightly from the pot sides. Stir in butter and Parmesan; season with salt and pepper.
4. Fill a shallow skillet with water, add white vinegar, and bring to a gentle simmer. Create a gentle whirlpool with a spoon, then slide eggs into the center one at a time. Poach 3–4 minutes until whites are set but yolks remain runny.
5. Pour polenta into a bowl, top with roasted tomatoes and poached eggs, and garnish with fresh basil.
meal.tip: Polenta can be made up to 2 days ahead and stored in the fridge; reheat gently with a splash of broth over low heat while you roast fresh tomatoes and poach eggs on race morning. The hot polenta won't spike your blood sugar as hard as simple carbs, making it ideal for sustained endurance.
